title: The canon-git divergence check belongs in intent doctor: every Intent project has the exposure, bin/.devbin reaches only this one
body:
**RECORDED, NOT BUILT** (vc, 2026-09-04). The check is landing at `bin/.devbin/cmd/` under the same ruling; this issue records that `bin/.devbin/` reaches THIS estate alone, while the exposure belongs to every Intent project.

## The exposure

**Filing an issue writes the store and the disk atomically and correctly. Git is a separate, human-gated act, and nothing reports the divergence.** (cc's wording, adopted -- the earlier framing *the store and git disagree* pointed a remedy at consistency machinery that is already sound. Store-versus-disk was driven at 214/214, perfect both ways.)

So an issue is filed, resolvable by every verb, present on disk, and absent from git -- and behaves completely normally until someone clones, or a fold goes looking.

**This is not local to Intent.** `issues add` writes store and disk everywhere; git is a separate act everywhere. Every project running Intent has the same exposure, which is why `bin/.devbin/cmd/` is the wrong durable home and `intent doctor` is the right one.

## Measured here, 2026-09-04

Four instances inside one day: `0230` and `0231` (ic), `0232` (cc), `0233` (vc). All four were found BY HAND -- `0230`/`0231` and `0233` reached git only through remediation commits whose subject lines literally say *was never in git*. **A class that has only ever been detected by hand is the strongest available evidence that nothing automatic is watching.**

## The mechanism is WHETHER, not WHEN

The four ids ran consecutively, which invites a temporal explanation -- *something about that window*. **It is refuted:** all six issues in the range `0230`-`0235` carry `created: 2026-09-04`, and `0234` and `0235` landed from inside the same window.

**The discriminator is whether the issue was the SUBJECT of a commit or a side-artefact of one.** `0234` and `0235` are named in their commits' subject lines -- they were the work. The other four were filed while doing something else, so no commit was ever about them and nothing swept them in.

**Consequence: the exposure is a HABIT, not a date.** Every node files issues in passing, so the rate does not decay -- it is constant, and a remedy keyed to a window, a session, or a node would miss every instance. This is the argument for a check that runs on a schedule rather than one that is remembered.

## What the check must do

**Both directions.** Store-has / git-lacks is the direction measured here. **Git-has / disk-lacks is the one that bites on a clone**, and it is the direction nobody has been bitten by yet -- which is the only reason it is not on anyone's list (ic asked for both; the arm is labelled as untested-in-anger rather than as hypothetical).

**And it must carry a positive control.** The population currently agrees except for one file, and an all-green sweep over an agreeing population cannot distinguish a working check from a broken one. The landed version injects a disk-only name and asserts the check goes red.

## Why this is NOT `intent doctor` today, and why it is not a duplicate

vc nearly refused the `bin/.devbin/cmd/` placement on Highlander grounds, on the reading that `intent doctor` already reports canon disagreement, and drove it instead: **doctor's residues are model-INTERNAL contradictions** -- a canon file asserting two things that cannot both be true, of which three are live in this tree. **This axis is disk-versus-git.** Different axis, no second home. Nothing in the tree compares `.canon` to git; the search returned zero.

## Not to be built now

Filed so the durable home is on the record whether or not it is reached before the tag.
